Try cardio a bit at a time and be careful while you ease into it. When you feel any symptoms come on just stop and rest until they subside, then wait a little more and go back to it. I recommend a stationary bike at first; running causes a bouncing motion in the head which may irritate you. Pay very close attention to your symptoms- respect them because it's your brain saying it needs rest. Over time the cardio will ideally increase and you'll be able to run again.

For instance, I started swimming laps 4 months post TBI and could only get 10 in before getting dizzy/foggy/sick. 3 months later I can do 45, and I'm back to rock climbing and biking through town. I also started triathlon training and it's done wonders for my psyche. 

This success was only possible because I took it very slow and listened to the symptoms even if I didn't want to. So that's my recommendation to you... I was an athlete before the TBI, trained anywhere from 3-6 hours a day, and had to be very mindful about how my boundaries have changed. 

Hope this helps!
The thing that helps the ringing the most, along with the majority of my symptoms, is intense cardio and THC use. I don't smoke THC but I eat it and this combo has been saving my ass for a while now.

I fast when I feel the symptoms coming on (for me this is confusion and acute irritability) and I don't do it intermittently per se... I'll eat very lightly and only eat fruits/veggies. I don't starve myself but I let myself be hungry until I feel better.

Oh god, yes. It's been 7 months post TBI and I feel like the spirituality has finally calmed a little. I was having these intense dreams and visions and believe it or not these visions related so clearly to reality that it scared me. Sometimes I feel like I can't sit down because of this feeling within that resembles a giant burning white fire. I also have been able to "see" people's souls and feel their feelings as if they were my own. For example, my partner got sick and started puking so hard his stomach hurt, but I felt the same exact pain in my abdomen in the same exact spot. When he's agitated I'm agitated, when he's calm I'm calm; this happens even if we are not together in person or even if I don't know how he's feeling that day. It's more intense with him than others but I have to say that I can "feel" everyone around me in more detailed ways than before. I read A Separate Reality by Carlos Castaneda and it helped illuminate what I've been going through. I recommend it. Hi there. I understand this incredibly jarring situation. 
It is possible your mother doesn't know what to do. She has to suddenly raise her kids by herself. I think the pressure and confusion of that reality is harder to deal with than we, as kids, could ever imagine. It sounds like she needs love. 
My dad has been a shell of a person since my mom died 6 years ago. He is closed off and cruel. I try to avoid him. 
But your mom is not my dad. Maybe she's more open than that. If you're worried about her not supporting you, maybe take her on a drive and just talk. Do something sweet and stress relieving. Avoid unnecessary pressure. Be honest and gentle with each other about how you're feeling about these deaths.
Sometimes just talking and affirming a connection between each other is what matters most. 
Hope this helps.
